newsitem.title: FRANCE: Juncker says plans list of taxes to be harmonised.
newsitem.headline: Juncker says plans list of taxes to be harmonised.

text.p: Luxembourg Prime Minister Jean-Claude Juncker said on Wednesday he wanted to work on ironing out tax quirks in the European Union during the country's presidency of the EU in the second half of this year.
He told a business lunch that during the Luxembourg presidency he wanted the EU to draw up a list of tax quirks in the EU in preparation for Economic and Monetary Union.
"It seems clear to me that the logic of EMU will force us to bring our taxation closer together," he said.
But he said he did not believe this should be limited to savings taxes only.

Luxembourg has come under fire from some of its European partners for its generous savings tax regime, which draws savers from neighbouring countries and allowed it to build a thriving banking centre.

European Union finance ministers have suggested they look at bringing taxation closer together in preparation for monetary union, but have so far made little or no progress on the issue, especially since tax decisions must be taken unanimously.
Juncker said the EU would also have to look at anomalies in social and labour conditions. "We have to have a basis of minimum social rights," he said.
